subject: Civil Engineering
title: Drift: How Far Buildings Sway
description: A 60-second lesson on Drift: How Far Buildings Sway.

hook.text: A skyscraper sways 3 feet during an earthquake. If the floors shift too much, walls crack.

buildup.text: Interstory drift is the relative movement between adjacent floors — the critical measure.

discovery.text: Codes limit drift to about 2% of story height — roughly 3 inches for a typical floor.

twist.text: Non-structural elements — glass walls, pipes — fail at drift levels below structural limits.

climax.text: Performance-based design sets different drift limits for frequent vs. rare earthquakes.

punchline.text: The building can sway, but the walls between floors can't keep up. Drift is the limit.

quiz.question: Why are drift limits important in seismic design?
options: Excessive drift makes occupants dizzy during normal wind conditions
Too much relative movement between floors damages walls, glass, and building systems
Drift limits determine how many floors a building can have

details.summary: Story drift is the horizontal displacement of one floor relative to the floor below during an earthquake, expressed as a ratio of displacement to story height. Excessive drift damages partitions, facades, and mechanical systems even when the structural frame remains intact.
details.whyItMatters: Drift limits protect both non-structural building components and structural stability. Non-structural damage from excessive drift causes the majority of economic losses in moderate earthquakes.
takeaways: Story drift ratio is lateral displacement divided by story height
Code limits range from 1% for sensitive buildings to 2.5% for flexible frames
Non-structural damage from drift causes most earthquake economic losses

faq.question: How much drift can a typical building tolerate before structural damage occurs?
faq.answer: Concrete frames typically sustain structural damage above 1 to 2% drift. Steel moment frames can tolerate 3 to 4% drift before significant damage. However, non-structural elements like glass curtain walls, interior partitions, and piping systems begin to crack and break at 0.

faq.question: Why is controlling drift important for adjacent buildings?
faq.answer: If adjacent buildings sway in opposite directions during an earthquake and the gap between them is insufficient, they collide, causing pounding damage. Building codes require minimum separation distances based on the combined maximum expected drifts of both buildings.
